issue_title: BlockedMessageLib advertises a bidirectional interface while intentionally blocking one side
operational_risk: OApps or operators may configure a library believing both directions are supported and later hit blocked receive behavior.
recommended_mitigation: Expose narrower capability flags for intentionally blocked libraries.
Add regression tests asserting advertised interface support matches implemented callable behavior.
root_cause: Capability/interface metadata is not aligned with the library implementation semantics.
source_name: Code4rena 2026-04 LayerZero Stellar Endpoint final report
source_report_section: Low / non-critical findings: BlockedMessageLib advertises send-and-receive interface without receive implementation
summary: A blocked/default message library can report capabilities that imply send and receive support even though the receive side is intentionally unavailable. This is an integration and configuration-footgun finding rather than direct fund loss.
when_it_could_escalate: A router or endpoint trusts the advertised capability as an authorization gate and then executes an unintended code path.
Misadvertised receive support can permanently strand messages or funds in a permissionless way.
why_not_medium_or_high: The mismatch can mislead integrators or operators, but by itself does not show an unauthorized message execution, fund loss, or durable protocol insolvency path.
